subject: Dedicated capacity — traffic census & prompt/response breakdown (Lumina)
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Kai Huang <kai@lumina.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 4 Jun 2027 16:05:00 -0400
Subject: Dedicated capacity — traffic census & prompt/response breakdown (Lumina)

Hi Kai,

Great to meet yesterday — thanks for the time. As we discussed, to size a recommended Dedicated (reserved) fleet for Lumina we need a short traffic census from your engineering/product team so our pre-sales model can map throughput, latency and cost. I captured the minimum fields below; filling the CSV I attached (lumina_traffic_snapshot.csv) will let us run a quick projection and propose a SKU mix.

Quick asks (can be rough):
- Primary workloads (names + short description) and estimated % of traffic per workload.
- Average prompt length and average response length (tokens or words) per workload.
- Concurrent sessions / active connections during peak 95th percentile and typical sustained concurrency.
- Peak QPS and expected sustained QPS by daypart (UTC) — list your burst windows.
- Latency SLOs (p50/p95/p99 target) per workload and whether p99 is a hard requirement.
- Session duration distribution (e.g., many short chats vs long multi-turn sessions).
- Any heavy generation vs classification/embedding mix (approx %).
- Security/compliance constraints we should know up front (VPC, data retention limits, SOC2 evidence requests).

If you prefer, I can run a 30–45 minute session with your engineering lead to walk through the CSV — we can also accept telemetry export (Prometheus/CloudWatch) if you have that.

I attached a one-page presales_sizer guide that explains how we convert these fields into GPU SKUs and autoscaling bands. If you can circle back by EOD Monday (US business days) we’ll turn around a draft fleet plan within 48 hours.

Thanks — talk soon.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0146

Attachments: lumina_traffic_snapshot.csv (CSV), redwood_presales_sizer.pdf (overview)
From: Kai Huang <kai@lumina.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 4 Jun 2027 18:42:00 -040:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — traffic census & prompt/response breakdown (Lumina)

Hi Soojin — thanks, this is helpful. I pulled together a quick pass below and attached the CSV you sent back with values filled. High level: we have two production surfaces — Conversational Assist (customer chat) and Batch Summarization for enterprise jobs.

1) Conversational Assist (70% traffic)
- Avg prompt length: 28 tokens
- Avg response length: 120 tokens
- Peak concurrent sessions (95th): 18,500
- Sustained concurrency (typical): 4,200
- Peak QPS: 2,900 (burst windows: 15:00–16:00 UTC and 01:00–01:20 UTC)
- Latency targets: p95 < 300ms, p99 < 900ms (p99 is soft but we prefer < 1s)
- Session durations: median 55s; ~12% sessions > 5min (multi-turn)
- Generation vs classification: 92% generation, 8% light classification

2) Batch Summarization (30% traffic)
- Avg prompt length: 540 tokens (documents)
- Avg response length: 220 tokens
- Peak concurrent jobs: 140 (jobs spawn parallel workers)
- Sustained concurrency: 40
- Peak QPS (per-worker effective): 65
- Latency targets: p95 < 2s for worker-level; job-level can be minutes
- Jobs typically run on schedule windows (03:00–05:00 UTC)

Security: we need VPC/private deployment for the Reserved fleet; SOC2 in progress (expected completion Q4). Procurement is cc'd on this thread (procurement@lumina.ai) to align on contracting later.

Let me know if the numbers as-is are sufficient for a draft estimate — happy to jump on a call.

-Kai

Attachment: lumina_traffic_snapshot.csv (filled)
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Kai Huang <kai@lumina.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 5 Jun 2027 09:18:00 -040:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — traffic census & prompt/response breakdown (Lumina)

Thanks Kai — this is great and much appreciated. A couple quick clarifying items so our projection matches Lumina's operational model:

1) For Conversational Assist: is the reported "Peak QPS 2,900" measured at the API request level (1 request = 1 prompt/response), or is that end-user rate after client-side multiplexing? Also, is the 2,900 an aggregate across global regions or primarily US?

2) Token accounting: are your token counts counted post-tokenization (i.e., the count used by your current provider) or estimated by word-based heuristics? Small differences in prompt tokenization change GPU perf numbers.

3) For Batch Summarization: when you say "jobs spawn parallel workers" — are workers colocated (single host) or distributed (parallel across many pods)? If distributed, average workers per job?

4) Session affinity: do you use long-lived WebSocket sessions (KV cache reuse) for Conversational Assist? If yes, what's average cache size in tokens per session? That affects memory and KV cache planning.

If you can answer 1–4 quickly we’ll lock an initial SKU mix and run simulation for expected p95/p99 tail costs. If it's easier, we can schedule a 30-min call Monday morning — Marissa, can you take the runbook if they want a walkthrough?

— Soojin
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Kai Huang <kai@lumina.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, procurement@lumina.ai
Date: Sun, 6 Jun 2027 13:23:00 -040:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — traffic census & prompt/response breakdown (Lumina)

Hi Kai — looping in procurement and Laura from our operations team. Short answers to Soojin's points:

- The 2,900 QPS is at the API request level (one request = one prompt/response) and is US-heavy — ~82% of that comes from US regional traffic during peak window.
- Token counts in the CSV are from your current provider's tokenization but we've added a +5% buffer in our model to account for minor tokenization drift.
- Batch Summarization workers are distributed across pods; average workers per job is 8, with a median job fan-out of 6–10 workers.
- Conversational Assist uses WebSocket sessions with KV cache reuse; average cache size ~1.6k tokens, with a 95th percentile session history of ~4.5k tokens.

Next steps: we've ingested your filled CSV and will produce an initial Dedicated fleet proposal that includes: expected GPU SKUs, reserved capacity sizing (sustained and burst headroom), expected monthly token cost, and a p95/p99 latency simulation for the Conversational Assist workload. Expect the draft by EOD Tuesday — I'll include a short appendix with recommended autoscaling bands and fallback model variants for cost control.

If procurement needs a vendor worksheet or contract template sooner, Laura can provide the enterprise procurement packet (cc'd).

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Pre-Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Attachments referenced: redwood_presales_sizer.pdf (explainer), vendor_contract_packet.docx (procurement packet)
